chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I feed a beggar whom I do not know is a Muslim.' He said, 'Yes, give to the one you do not know with a disposition of guardianship/affinity and not enmity towards the Truth.'
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says, 'And speak to people in good words.'
And do not feed the one who has set up opposition to something of the Truth or called to something of the Falsehood.'
ai.seo_question: How should one choose recipients of charity based on their relationship to the Truth and falsehood?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refines the criteria for distributing charity by linking it to theological alignment rather than mere identity, advising to give to those who are neutral or aligned with the Truth while withholding from those who actively promote falsehood. This ruling underscores the Shia concept of *Wilayah* in social transactions, where charity serves as a means of supporting the cause of truth against falsehood. The reference to 'speaking good to people' highlights the ethical demeanor required even in the act of giving, ensuring the charity is received with grace and dignity.
